prompt: Some people think that machine translation is highly developed in today's society. Therefore, it is not necessary for students to learn a foreign language. What's your opinion?
essay:
In the modern world , technology is used to convert information from one language to another. Thus, it  may be senseless to learn another tongue. I strongly believe that this is not correct. I will explain this by looking at natural speech and quick talks.

Starting with fluent speakers, not only is listening to them like a melody, but it is also connected to a rhythm. For instance, when you are sitting in a coffee shop and listening to native speakers, it completely differs from a digital phone assistant. A phone app may give the right words but miss a joke, a polite form, or a sad tone.  A machine cannot replace this human link, but students can learn it by studying without relying on a device.

Secondly, people need to reply quickly in real conversations, and translation apps may slow them down. Not only does a conversation without a computer help appear more natural, but it also enables two or more speakers to interrupt each other in no time. In addition,  it is possible to give your opinion straightforwardly in the discussion. Despite the fact of not being reliable on devices, it ensures to continue with ongoing debates. Speaking the language helps people explain their ideas and answer at the same time.

To summarise, even though the computers and software are on a very high level for translations, artificial intelligence is not as good as human connection and fast, natural talk yet. So, I definitely believe that translation tools are useful, but they cannot fully take the place of speech learning. For this reason, it is highly recommended for young people to invest in communication skills, as they can not be replaced with machinery.
